clues.text: An artwork by this man was made in accordance with the principles laid out in book 3 of De Architectura.
This artist painted Cecilia Gallerani holding an unusually large, white animal in the oil portrait on wood namedLady with an Ermine.
In one fresco by this man, St. Thomas raises his index figure in doubt as the central figure stretches his hands over a table.
This artist created The Virgin of the Rocks using sfumato, a shading technique that created a mysterious atmosphere, which he also used in a portrait of Francesco del Gioconda’s wife.
A sketch by this artist features a scraggly-haired man with four arms and four legs inscribed inside of a circle.
A male nude is inscribed within a circle and a square in this artist’s Vitruvian Man.

This artist painted threespots in a non-reflective crystal ball in the hand of Jesus in one painting, and painted a delicate veil onto Lisa del Giocondo, whose eyebrows have wornaway, in a portrait with an enigmatic smile.
This artist of Madonna of the Rocks created a fresco in which the Twelve Disciples are grouped into threes, and Judas can be seen holding a bag of silver.
This man depicted the wife of Francesco del Giocondo smiling mysteriously in another painting.
Name this Italian renaissance painter ofSalvatorMundiand the Mona Lisa.

clues.text: Two composers from this country who published the Cantiones Sacrae shared a 21-year monopoly on polyphonic music.
Swagger portraits in the “grand manner” became popular in this country after an artist published the treatise Discourses on Art.
A composer from this country used the descending motif (read slowly) long A, short G, short F, long E to begin each of a collection of seven pieces based on a pavan (puh-VAAN).
In another painting from this country, Mary comforts a young Christ who has cut his hand in Joseph’s carpentry shop.

A composer from this country depicted a bulldog falling into a river in the movement “G.R.S.” A composer from this country gently parodied Dora Penny’s stutter in the movement Dorabella.The composer’s friends are “pictured within” a work from this country that includes the movement “Nimrod,” the Enigma Variations.
In a painting from this country, figures representing Pity and Terror appear behind a model portraying the Tragic Muse, Sarah Siddons.
One artist from this country depicted a dog standing near a river by Willy Lott’s cottage toward which a cart is being pulled.
A composer from this country wrote five marches often played at graduation ceremonies.
Name this home country of the artists of Rain, Steam, and Speed and The Hay Wain, J.M.W Turner and John Constable.
Name this home country of Ralph (rayf) Vaughn Williams, who portrayed its capital in A London Symphony.
This artist painted a woman in a blue dress with one unfastened button in the ironically titled The Perfectionist.
This artist depicted a slave that wears a pink dress while storm clouds gather in his portrayal of a young, reluctant George Washington refusing to give an axe to his father.
He argued for a truly national art in his manifesto Revolt against the City.
This artist depicted the title figure pulling back a red curtain to reveal a man holding a bent cherry tree next to a boy with an axe in Parson Weems’ Fable.
An open curtain reveals a historical figure with an ax in a work by this artist.
He also depicted a woman in a red and white woolen cap holding a hen in his Appraisal.

A satirical work by this artist depicts three “Tory Gals” in front of an Emanuel Leutze (“LOYT-zuh”) painting.Ella Watson was photographed in front of an American flag by Gordon Parks to parody a work by this artist, in whichhisdentist, Byron McKeeby, stands in front of the Dibble House holding a pitchfork.
This artist of Parson Weems' Fable and Daughters of Revolution also got his sister to pose sternly with his dentist in front of a red barn and a white house.
His most iconic work includes a red barn on the right of two grim-looking people in front of it.
Name this American regionalist artist who portrayed a pitchfork and two elders in American Gothic.
